title: Realizing finite normed coefficient fields and their module functors
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E$ be a finite normed field extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ whose norm restricts to the normalized $\ell$-adic norm, and fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its extended absolute value [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Put $A=\{x\in E:|x|\le1\}$, with its subspace topology. There exist a finite intermediate field $E'\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and an isometric $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra isomorphism $\sigma:E\xrightarrow{\sim}E'$ whose restriction identifies $A$ with $A'=\mathcal O_{E'}$. Condensation [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] identifies both coefficient inclusions $\underline A\to\underline E$ and $\underline{A'}\to\underline{E'}$ by these isomorphisms.

For each scheme $Z$ and $B=A,E$, put $B'=A',E'$ respectively and $B_Z=p_Z^*\underline B$, $B'_Z=p_Z^*\underline{B'}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Derived extension along the resulting ring-sheaf isomorphism defines an exact equivalence
$$J_Z^B:D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_Z))\xrightarrow{\sim}D(\operatorname{Mod}(B'_Z))$$
[sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. It and its inverse preserve each cohomological bound and bounded constructibility in the stratified locally finitely presented ring-object sense [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. For every scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, the ordinary ambient module derived direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] have natural comparison isomorphisms
$$J_Y^B Rf_{*,B}\cong Rf_{*,B'}J_X^B.$$
These comparisons use the coefficient maps induced from the point and identify the counit mates for the two coefficient presentations.

proof.text: Write $d=\dim_{\mathbf Q_\ell}E$. For each $x\in E$, the $d+1$ vectors $1,x,\ldots,x^d$ are linearly dependent, so $x$ satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed] to obtain a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-embedding $i:E\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Its image $E'=i(E)$ is a subfield containing $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $i$ corestricted to its image is an algebra isomorphism $\sigma:E\to E'$. The images of a basis of $E$ form a basis of $E'$, so $E'$ is finite of degree $d$.

source.place: Tag 09GU, lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure; elementary finite-dimensional reduction and image construction

proof.text: The function $x\mapsto|i(x)|$ is an absolute value on $E$: injectivity gives its zero condition, and multiplication and the triangle inequality follow by applying those in the algebraic closure. Since $i$ fixes $\mathbf Q_\ell$, it extends the normalized $\ell$-adic absolute value. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] it equals the supplied norm on $E$. Hence $|\sigma(x)-\sigma(y)|=|x-y|$ and both $\sigma$ and its inverse are continuous. The equation $|\sigma(x)|=|x|$ gives $\sigma(A)=\{z\in E':|z|\le1\}=A'$; restricting the isometry gives the required topological ring isomorphism $A\cong A'$.

proof.text: For $B=A,E$ let $s_B:B\cong B'$ be the isomorphism just constructed. On every profinite set $S$, postcomposition $h\mapsto s_B\circ h$ gives an isomorphism $C(S,B)\cong C(S,B')$, with inverse postcomposition by $s_B^{-1}$. These maps commute with restrictions and pointwise ring operations by [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. The square involving $A\hookrightarrow E$ and $A'\hookrightarrow E'$ commutes because $s_A$ is the restriction of $s_E$. Applying the functor $p_Z^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] gives ring isomorphisms $c_Z^B:B_Z\cong B'_Z$ and the commuting inclusion square on every scheme $Z$.

source.place: continuous-map formula and functoriality; sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, functoriality of pullback from the point

proof.text: Fix $B$ and omit its superscript. Put $R_Z=B_Z$, $S_Z=B'_Z$ and $P_Z=\operatorname{Res}_{c_Z^{-1}}$. Thus $P_ZM$ has the same underlying abelian sheaf, and $s\in S_Z$ acts as $c_Z^{-1}(s)$ on $M$. By clauses 4--5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], $P_Z$ and $\operatorname{Res}_{c_Z}$ are additive exact inverse equivalences, and $\operatorname{Ext}_{c_Z}\cong P_Z$. The latter isomorphism is $s\otimes m\mapsto c_Z^{-1}(s)m$, with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. The exact-functor result [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identifies its left derived functor with termwise $P_Z$, so the stated derived extension $J_Z^B$ is $D(P_Z)$. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] it is exact as a triangulated functor; termwise inverse scalar restriction gives its inverse on the localized categories.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; derived.tex Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; application to an invertible coefficient map

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $H^n(J_ZK)\cong P_ZH^n(K)$ for every integer $n$. The inverse equivalence has the same property. Since both functors carry zero to zero, every upper or lower cohomological bound is preserved in both directions. This proves the assertion about bounds without choosing a common bound in advance.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor; natural cohomology comparison recorded in the cited node

proof.text: For any stratum or covering morphism $g:W\to Z$, pulling back the action $R_Z\otimes M\to M$ precomposed with $c_Z^{-1}\otimes M$ gives the pulled-back action precomposed with $(g^*c_Z)^{-1}\otimes g^*M$. Thus inverse scalar restriction commutes with the $\operatorname{mapMod}(g^*)$ used in [def-sfb-constructible-module]. On $W$, clause 5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] identifies the regular $g^*R_Z$-module with the regular $g^*S_Z$-module by $g^*c_Z$. The exact additive equivalence therefore carries a presentation $(g^*R_Z)^m\to(g^*R_Z)^n\to M\to0$ to a presentation $(g^*S_Z)^m\to(g^*S_Z)^n\to P(M)\to0$, and its inverse does the reverse. This is precisely finite presentation in [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Consequently the same local covers in [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented] and the same finite stratification work for $M$ and its scalar transport. Applying this to each cohomology module from step 5 proves bounded constructibility in both directions by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible].

source.place: stratified locally finitely presented definition; explicit transport of each finite cokernel presentation

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$. Naturality in the coefficient ring of the point-pullback comparison defining $\alpha_f$ in [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] gives $c_X\alpha_{f,R}=\alpha_{f,S}f^*(c_Y)$. Taking adjoints gives $f_*(c_X)\eta_{f,R}=\eta_{f,S}c_Y$, since $\eta_f$ is the stated mate of $\alpha_f$. Using the inverse of this equality, the two actions of $S_Y$ on $f_*^{\mathrm{Ab}}M$ in $P_Y f_{*,R}M$ and $f_{*,S}P_XM$ coincide: both first send $s$ to $\eta_{f,R}(c_Y^{-1}s)$, then use the original action. By the explicit definition of module direct image in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], the identity of the underlying abelian sheaf is therefore a natural module isomorphism $\gamma_M:P_Y f_{*,R}M\cong f_{*,S}P_XM$.

source.place: naturality of alpha from point pullback and its mate eta; explicit module pushforward definition in sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-comap-preserves-k-injectives] to the condensed ring isomorphism $s_B^{-1}$. Its hypothesis holds for every scheme: extension along its pullback is inverse scalar restriction by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], hence an exact equivalence and in particular finite-limit preserving. Thus $P_X$ sends K-injectives to K-injectives. For a K-injective resolution $K\to I$, exactness makes $P_XK\to P_XI$ a quasi-isomorphism. The definition [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] consequently computes both sides of the required comparison on this one resolution: they are represented by $P_Y f_{*,R}I$ and $f_{*,S}P_XI$. Termwise $\gamma_I$ from step 7 is an isomorphism between them. It is natural in maps of K-injective complexes, hence in their homotopy category. The localization map from homotopy morphisms into a K-injective to derived morphisms is bijective by [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison]; together with resolution existence in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], this makes the K-injective homotopy category equivalent to the derived source category. This defines the natural isomorphism $J_Y Rf_{*,R}\cong Rf_{*,S}J_X$ on the ordinary unbounded categories.

source.place: flat restriction preserves K-injectives; ambient total-derived computation in sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull

proof.text: For the corresponding ordinary inverse-image comparison, the tensor description in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] gives $\beta:P_X f_R^*\cong f_S^*P_Y$ by $a\otimes m\mapsto c_X(a)\otimes m$, with inverse $b\otimes m\mapsto c_X^{-1}(b)\otimes m$. The coefficient identity in step 7 is exactly the balancing relation needed for these maps. The adjunction unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ is fixed by this formula. The counit on a tensor $a\otimes n$ is the underlying inverse-image counit followed by scalar multiplication by $a$; on the changed side multiplication by $c_X(a)$ on $P_XM$ is, by definition, multiplication by $a$. Hence $\beta$ and $\gamma$ satisfy the actual unit and counit squares of the module adjunction; in particular $\gamma$ is its counit mate, with no choice of an unrelated adjunction.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict, and the explicit module pullback/pushforward adjunction in sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback; balanced tensor and counit calculation

proof.text: The $S$ coefficients are the admissible embedded finite-field or integer-ring coefficients, so [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] gives exactness of $f_S^*$. Since $P_X,P_Y$ are exact equivalences and $\beta$ is invertible, $f_R^*$ is exact too. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], their total left derived functors are the termwise functors, so all complexes can be used as the left resolving class. Apply [lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization] to the two module adjunctions: with any source complex and a K-injective target $I$, the derived Hom transpose is the localized ordinary Hom transpose. The same target $P_XI$ computes the changed adjunction by step 8. Step 9 makes these ordinary transposes agree, so their localized transposes agree as well. Therefore the derived $\gamma$ constructed in step 8 is the mate of the localized $\beta$ and identifies the derived counits. Equality holds on all derived morphisms by the localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. This proves the final normalization clause for both $B=A$ and $B=E$.

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors, and Tag 015F; normalization of transposes on K-injective targets as stated in lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization
